key_insight: The analysis establishes optimal error estimates with polynomial, rather than potentially exponential, dependence on inverse interface width for a mixed finite element scheme of the coupled Cahn–Hilliard–Navier–Stokes system.
engineering_relevance: These estimates strengthen confidence in finite element simulations of two-phase flows with thin diffuse interfaces.
method: Analyze a first-order convex-splitting mixed finite element scheme.
Combine H⁻¹ approximation properties of Ritz and Stokes projections with discrete Cahn–Hilliard spectral estimates.
Use a three-term discrete Gagliardo–Nirenberg inequality to reduce the degree of polynomial parameter dependence.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments test the theoretical results and demonstrate robustness across different interface-width parameters; the abstract provides no quantitative errors or convergence rates.
watch_item: Polynomial dependence still allows error constants to grow as interface width decreases; the abstract does not specify mesh or time-step restrictions.
paper_title: Optimal Error Estimates With Polynomial Dependence on $ε^{-1}$ for Mixed Finite Element Methods of the Cahn-Hilliard-Navier-Stokes System
